article.title: Nutrient-based subsidy rates cut 22% for phosphorus as global rock phosphate eases
article.text: The Cabinet approved nutrient-based subsidy rates for the coming season that cut the per-kilogram rate on phosphorus by twenty-two per cent and on potash by nine per cent, citing a decline in international rock phosphate and muriate of potash contract prices. Maximum retail prices for complex fertilisers remain under informal control, so a subsidy cut that runs ahead of the imported raw-material decline compresses the manufacturer's realised margin per bag rather than the farmer's cost. Coromandel International, which manufactures complex phosphatic fertilisers, and Chambal Fertilisers, whose portfolio is predominantly urea and therefore outside the nutrient-based regime, face very different exposure to the same notification. Urea remains on the separate fixed-price subsidy mechanism.
article.note: Two companies, one notification, and only one of them is actually inside the regime being changed. Sector membership is not exposure.

ground_truth.rationale: Both companies are fertiliser makers named by the same article; only one is inside the regime being changed. The verifier's explicit structural rejection removes the other before the gate ever sees it, and the rejection reason is recorded so a postmortem can tell 'the verifier said no' apart from 'the gate excluded it'.
